newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-REED FIRST HALF GROWTH DENTED BY STG.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-REED FIRST HALF GROWTH DENTED BY STG.

text.p: Shares in Reed Elsevier fell some six percent on Thursday after the Anglo-Dutch publisher said the strong pound had choked off growth in the first six months of the year.
Pre-tax profit rose only one percent to 419 million pounds ($671 million) as currency movements wiped 36 million pounds off earnings.
Co-chairman Nigel Stapleton said the second half impact was likely to be similar if the pound remained at current lev els.
Reed shares in London fell 39p to 591p by 1030 GMT in reaction to results at the bottom end of expectations.
Elsevier shares dropped 1.90 guilders (89 cents) to 35.40 in Amsterdam.
Sales fell one percent to 1.664 billion pounds, although they were six percent higher if measured at constant exchange rates.
The company said it remained 'positive' about prospects for the rest of 1997 and the longer-term. It noted profits were 10 percent higher at constant rates.
Stapleton put the market disappointment down to currency factors.
"The adjusting of forecasting for currencies tends to lag their actual movement and the impact is slightly larger than (share analysts) expected," he told Reuters.
Almost two thirds of Reed Elsevier's profit is derived from the U.S. dollar, Dutch guilder, Swiss franc and French franc but results are calculated in sterling.

Stapleton said Reed Elsevier was prepared to spend a further two billion dollars on acquisitions after committing around one billion dollars so far in "Growth by acquisition continues to be an important part of our strategic agenda...We are well up to speed with what might be available," he said.
Reed Elsevier has sold sold many of its consumer businesses such as local newspapers, in order to focus on the provision of information in fields like science, business and the legal profession.
It confirmed that it planned to dispose of its remaining consumer book publishing activities, which comprise children's and illustrated books.
Reed Elsevier's spending commitment takes account of the $447 million acquisition of U.S. business publisher Chilton, which is expected to be completed shortly.
Other big acquisitions this year include a $320 million deal for MDL Information Systems, a U.S. scientific software and information database company.
Reed Elsevier said its rate of margin growth would be constrained by the higher investment in electronic publishing initiatives and continuing difficulties at its Reed Travel Group arm.
Hard copy revenues from the travel arm are in decline and the company has embarked on a two-year investment programme to develop its online business.
